text: The two story files 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/RWB P4 AD003 APP Scope per role v1.md and RWB P4 AD003 CON Scope per role - contract v1.md, and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD003-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD003-CON.json, all already present in the tree and written by the parallel Work Package B-P4-02 for the same two slices of legacy RWB-AD-003, stand as the deliverable of B2-P4-002: they are not rewritten, not versioned to v2, not duplicated, and their missing values stay registered once as CG-B-P4-02-AD003-1 and CG-B-P4-02-AD003-2 with ASM-B-P4-02-AD003-1 to ASM-B-P4-02-AD003-8. Their metadata, their 19 sections, AC1 and AC2 of RWB-AD-003 with the origin tag on the APP file, the seven (new, D-RCV-60) criteria of the CON file, the four legacy test case IDs TC-AD-003-01 to TC-AD-003-04 with the Level column, the section 12 tables and the citation set are kept unchanged, and B2-P4-002 registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding.
why: The Work Package names the two story files and the two fragments as its outputs and every one of them already exists with complete content, because the plan issues two Work Packages for one legacy key (B-P4-02 with fanout 5 and B2-P4-002 with fanout 0). Root AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids editing a file that already exists and forbids writing a path outside the 'Write only' block, so the next-version copy that rule 1 would otherwise ask for cannot be created here (a v2 file is not a listed output), and rule 13 forbids stopping the run. The existing artefacts were therefore read, verified against Template and Rules v1 R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9 and kept, and the collision is recorded as one gap row and this row, in the same way as the parallel B2-P1-001 and B2-P1-014 findings and the other B2 collisions of this run.
read: _work/msr/wp/B-P4-02.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-002.md (the same four output paths); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slices RWB-P4-AD003-CON in CG-W4 and RWB-P4-AD003-APP in L-P4-C); _work/msr/gaps/B-P4-02-AD003.part.jsonl and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P4-02-AD003.part.jsonl (the citations the four artefacts carry); _work/msr/status.json (no entry for either Work Package); the two story files and two fragments themselves, checked for the R8.1 header, a D-RCV-60 change-log row with the tool line, 20 metadata rows in the R7.1 order, the 19 section headings in order, the AC origin tags, the R7.2 Level column, tables 12.1 to 12.9 and the R9 placeholder form; the P4 context pack for the service row, schema, REST base, topic and queue; root AGENTS.md rules 1, 2, 9 and 13
applied_in: B2-P4-002: the four artefacts left unchanged, no value re-registered and no row duplicated; _work/msr/gaps/B2-P4-002.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/assumptions/B2-P4-002.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/editlog/B2-P4-002.md
confirm: Delivery lead and the stage B2 coordinator at the wave 4 batch close, when the plan is de-duplicated and the B-P4-02 title is closed with its edit log row
impact: If the coordinator instead wants B2-P4-002 to own the two files, they must be rewritten from legacy RWB-AD-003 with a new set of CG and ASM citations of the form CG-B2-P4-002-n, which invalidates the 11 identifiers the delivered artefacts cite and the cross-references the sibling files RWB P4 AD002, AD004, AD005 and AD006 carry, and gains no content beyond a shorter file (the style aim of 20-25 KB per file in the Work Package is not met: the two files are 62,925 and 50,754 bytes); if that is chosen, the two B-P4-02 AD003 gap rows and its eight assumption rows must be retired rather than numbered beside the new set at step D1.
